name: Coding quality rubric (C6 / C7 / C8 / C9)
name_zh: 编码质量评分标准（C6 / C7 / C8 / C9）
summary: Pass/fail stays exactly as before (D1: the source benchmark's hidden tests). On top, an LLM judge grades 3 common items (Readability, Maintainability, Robustness; meanings from C3 D3-D5) and 1-2 case-specific items per case (evaluation/rubrics/tasks/<ID>.json), each perfect / accept / bad.
pass_fail: D1, unchanged: a trial passes iff the source benchmark's hidden-test verifier passes (FrontierSWE: score >= pass_threshold).

judge.calls: one per trial; answers all items
judge.sees: task prompt, reference solution (for comparison only), the agent's code change, a condensed action log, its final message, the hidden-test outcome
judge.when: run_benchmark --quality full grades each trial right after it finishes; the default --quality machine records only the validity audit, and the judge is run later with evaluation/quality_grader.py (answers cached per trial in judge_v3_<judge>.json)

na.meaning: no basis (e.g. no code change); excluded

common_items.name: Readability
common_items.question: Is the agent's code easy to read: intent-revealing names, formatting consistent with the existing code, docstrings/comments where logic is non-obvious?

criteria.perfect: Intent-revealing naming that reads like natural language; formatting consistent with the existing codebase; public interfaces documented; complex logic has inline comments (minor documentation gaps on non-obvious logic are still perfect).
criteria.accept: Mostly readable, but some cryptic names (temp, data1, v) or complex logic without comments.
criteria.bad: Inconsistent naming/casing, large undocumented blocks, confusing layout, or cryptic naming throughout.

caps: Single-letter variable names in business logic (not loop counters) -> at most accept.

common_items.name: Maintainability
common_items.question: Is the change well structured and easy to change later: separation of concerns, short single-responsibility functions, reuse of existing helpers, no copy-pasted logic, no dead code / debug leftovers?

criteria.perfect: Clear separation of concerns; short single-responsibility functions (mostly < 30 lines); reuses existing helpers and patterns; loose coupling; no copy-pasted logic, dead code or debug output.
criteria.accept: Standard structure, but some details leak across layers, a few functions are monolithic, there is some duplicated logic, or leftover dead code / debug output.
criteria.bad: Monolithic functions (> 80 lines), high complexity or deep nesting (4+ levels), systemic copy-paste, global mutable state, or tight coupling.

caps: A single new file > 500 lines -> at most accept.

common_items.name: Robustness
common_items.question: Is the code defensive: specific exceptions handled, resources managed safely, inputs validated at boundaries, no magic constants, errors never silently swallowed?

criteria.perfect: Defensive throughout: specific exceptions handled, safe resource management, input validation at boundaries, no (or < 2 minor) magic constants, concurrency-safe where relevant.
criteria.accept: Errors are handled, but generic catch-all blocks are common, some magic constants, or 1-2 edge cases lack validation.
criteria.bad: Errors silently swallowed (bare except / except Exception: pass), resource-leak risks, no input validation, or hardcoded credentials.

caps: Bare except: / except Exception: pass in business logic -> at most accept.
Errors silently swallowed on data-mutation paths -> bad.

case_items: 1-2 per case in evaluation/rubrics/tasks/<ID>.json: task-specific questions (e.g. edge cases the tests don't cover, API compatibility), LLM judge, perfect / accept / bad.

aggregation.quality_score: 100 * mean of the item scores (3 common + 1-2 case items, equal weight; n/a excluded)
aggregation.per_case_model: pass rate (D1) and mean quality score over the trials
aggregation.final_score: none: pass rate (D1) and quality (D2) are reported separately, not combined

validity_audit: Not a rubric item: quality_grader also checks the action log / diff for access to the hidden tests, reference solution or entry files, downloads of the upstream fix, and test tampering. A confirmed finding marks the trial invalid (valid = false; its pass/fail is unreliable and it should be re-run); ambiguous findings (only listing benchmark folders, changed lines in existing tests, writes to /tests) are listed as provisional and do not invalidate the trial.
human_review: Spot-check judge answers (tools/quality_report.py lists a fixed 5% sample in results/README_quality.md). Overrides go in results/quality_overrides.json ({"<run>/<trial>": {"<item id>": {"level": ..., "reviewer": ..., "note": ...}}}) and are applied on the next grading pass.
